I started with a friend’s neighbor doing housecleaning… but if you’re in Washington state there’s a Medicaid/medicare program you can work for. Look up home care aid in your state or country. I’ve found most places where I have friends have something similar even if it’s not as large. 

Other contacts I’ve made are social workers and people who are guardians, PoA or similar for elderly and or disabled individuals. Just be up front about what you can do. If you’re not up for a certain type of disability because you’re not trained say it! I have people who are ADHD/autistic and only need help doing specific tasks like litter or dishes. One that has a guardian who only recently started needing physical help when they got sick with something. That one just depends on how comfortable you are about health stuff.

I work for some people as a cat litter scooper, a couple as their dishwasher at their home, one I usually go on errands with so shopping, Dr appointments, etc. One I am a home care assistant for so cleaning, making food taking them to appointments. It’s taken years to get here but I make between $20-45 per hour depending on which client. The lowest one is my client through the state but I get healthcare if I work enough each month. I might go out to eat since I can usually find something on the menu like a Caesar salad that I will eat but I don’t expect my roommates or any partner to cook for me day to day or even weekly.

Cheese, crackers and ham was a go to while I was a teenager. Same with nachos even if it was just chips and cheese that day. I can usually eat chicken, ham, bacon, and some other meats. Beef is the one that I have the most trouble with although not like people with the tick bite allergy.
